question: What is the main question this lesson asks you to investigate?
options: A)  How fast can a robot run a race?
B)  How does a real mouse solve a maze compared to a robot?
C)  Which programming language is the best?
D)  How do you build a robot from scratch?

question: A robot uses instincts the same way a mouse does.
options: A) True
B) False

question: The robot turned RIGHT at a junction but should have turned LEFT. Which fix is correct?
options: A)  Delete all the robot's instructions and start over
B)  Change the 'turn right' instruction to 'turn left' at that specific step
C)  Make the robot go faster so it corrects itself
D)  Add more sensors to the robot

question: A mouse uses trial-and-error. A robot follows a fixed recipe. Which statement BEST explains when trial-and-error is the better approach?
options: A)  When you already know exactly what to do
B)  When the environment is brand new and you need to explore it
C)  When speed matters more than accuracy
D)  When you have a perfect map of the maze

question: Why did the robot run the maze a SECOND time much faster than the first time?
options: A)  Someone upgraded its wheels
B)  It memorized the correct path during its first exploration run
C)  It got lucky the second time
D)  The maze got easier

question: The 'left-hand-on-the-wall' strategy means: always keep your hand touching the left wall as you move. What kind of agent behavior does this strategy represent?
options: A)  Trial-and-error (trying random paths)
B)  A fixed rule that always runs the same way
C)  Learning from mistakes
D)  Multi-agent teamwork

question: When you build a BlocklyTM program to solve the maze, you are doing what a robot's programmer does.
options: A) True
B) False

question: The mechanical maze's ball moves while you are trying to guide it. Compared to the paper maze, this makes the mechanical maze:
options: A)  More observable
B)  Less fully observable AND more dynamic
C)  A multi-agent environment
D)  A known environment

question: In a KNOWN environment, the agent:
options: A)  Has to explore and discover the rules as it goes
B)  Already knows all the rules and what will happen for each action
C)  Cannot see any of the environment
D)  Must work with a partner

question: You are solving the paper maze. You can see every wall and path before you start. APPLY the concept: this maze is:
options: A)  Partially Observable
B)  Dynamic
C)  Fully Observable
D)  Multi-Agent

question: Two robots working TOGETHER to map an unknown building is an example of:
options: A)  Single-Agent competitive
B)  Multi-Agent cooperative
C)  Multi-Agent competitive
D)  Single-Agent cooperative

question: Which of the following is the BEST example of a DYNAMIC environment?
options: A)  A completed jigsaw puzzle sitting on a table
B)  A written math test you are taking alone
C)  A soccer match where players keep moving
D)  A library where all books stay on their shelves

question: Which statement BEST summarizes what makes AI different from natural intelligence?
options: A)  AI is always faster than natural intelligence
B)  AI is smarter than humans in every situation
C)  AI follows programmed rules rather than thinking and feeling like a living creature
D)  AI cannot learn anything new

question: A dog sniffs out a hidden toy. A robot uses a camera to find the same toy. What is the correct parallel?
options: A)  Dog uses eyes; robot uses nose
B)  Dog uses its nose (smell); robot uses a camera (vision sensor)
C)  Both use cameras
D)  Dog uses whiskers; robot uses a microphone

question: An AI gives a student the wrong homework answer. The student submits it without checking. Who bears MOST responsibility?
options: A)  Only the AI
B)  Only the programmer
C)  The programmer AND the student share responsibility, though differently
D)  Only the company that made the AI
